newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israelis wounded in West Bank blast - army.
newsitem.headline: Two Israelis wounded in West Bank blast - army.

text.p: A roadside bomb blew up near an Israeli civilian bus in the West Bank on Wednesday, wounding two Israeli paramilitary policemen in a jeep guarding the vehicle, the army said.
The blast occurred in Israeli-occupied territory on the outskirts of the Palestinian-ruled city of Nablus.

"Two border policemen were slightly to moderately wounded when a bomb exploded near their jeep while they were accompanying a bus of worshippers who visited Joseph's Tomb in Nablus," the army said in a statement.
Joseph's Tomb is a Jewish shrine Israel controls in the West Bank city under interim peace deals with the PLO. Israel Radio said the bus was travelling to the nearby Jewish settlement of Alon Moreh.
The attack came as Israel's defence minister and a top PLO official met near Tel Aviv for talks, with U.S. and Egyptian mediation, on resuming formal peace negotiations.
Tensions have been high in the West Bank since Israel began work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
